LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyRansom: Offers for captives both ways, the game's ransom demand by messenger without a comms console, exchanges at the gate.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyRansom_Tip: Two to six days after one of a people is taken prisoner, if their people want them back (their leader, a notable or a notable's kin always; anyone else six times in ten from a people at peace, three in ten from a hostile one), their messenger comes to the gate, or a go-between of a people at peace with both, or their call at the comms console, with an offer of half to the whole of the captive's market value (half again for a notable, twice for their leader). Accept, ask for more, let them go for nothing, or keep them; refused three times, a grudge. Without a powered comms console, the game's own ransom demand for one of the colony's comes by their messenger at the game's rate and fee. Offer an exchange of theirs for one of the colony's they hold, and both walk at once at the gate. With a hostile people an exchange can be a trap: five times in a hundred, from twice to twenty times with the negotiator's ability, a band of theirs falls on the gate. Off: nothing new comes, and what is under way plays out.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyEnvoys: Their envoy as the colony's guest for a season, and the colony's own envoy at their town.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyEnvoys_Tip: A people at peace (goodwill 30 or more) whose envoy the colony knows may offer to send them for a season, at most once a year, one at a time at each home; or the colony asks by letter. Their envoy and an attendant stay as guests who do no work: they eat at the colony's table, sleep in a bed set aside for them, talk with its people, sit in at a council meeting, and send a letter home every five days. How the stay goes travels home with them: kept well, their head thinks better of the colony and may owe it a debt of honor; kept poorly, they feel slighted. The colony may send a colonist good with people (Social 6 or more) to live at their town for a season: their work is lost until they come home, their letters bring the town's news, and its notables come to think better of the colony. Off: nothing new is agreed, and a stay under way runs its season.
